units.function: Interactive selection of embedded or external PostgreSQL plus local backup schedule, retention and paths.
units.dependencyDirection: Prompt UI -> config types and ambient instance paths; no database/storage probe or service boundary.
units.keyDataModels: DatabaseConfig, connection string, embedded data/port and backup policy.
units.lifecycle: Select mode, collect URL or local path/port, collect backup settings, return config; cancellation exits the process.
units.testAssessment: No focused promptDatabase test was found. Completed onboard evidence covers eight broad setup cases but not external credentials/TLS, adversarial validation, cancellation composability or backup restore.
units.designRationale: Provide a local-first default while exposing external PostgreSQL and backups in one setup flow.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs validated cloud/local database profiles, Secret references, TLS and restore-tested retention policy.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as a headless profile schema plus UI adapter. Accept Secret bindings instead of credential URLs, parse structurally and probe only with explicit consent/timeouts.
units.responsibilityConflict: Database and retention changes affect company evidence/data custody without a responsible operator or reviewed plan.
evidence: Existing onboard assessment reused; no focused prompt test found
units.securityFindings: HIGH: a credential-bearing PostgreSQL URL is collected with a normal text prompt and reused as a visible default, then returned as ordinary configuration. Validation checks only a postgres prefix, not URL grammar, TLS, host, credentials or database. Backup paths lack canonical/permission/encryption/capacity and restore validation.

units.function: Optionally chooses Anthropic or OpenAI and collects one masked API key into LlmConfig.
units.dependencyDirection: Prompt UI -> provider-specific config; no ModelProviderPort, Secret store or capability discovery.
units.keyDataModels: Provider enum and plaintext API key.
units.lifecycle: Opt in, select one of two vendors, collect nonempty password input, return key-bearing config.
units.testAssessment: No focused promptLlm test was found; completed onboard tests do not prove key custody, provider extensibility, model policy or cancellation isolation.
units.designRationale: Minimize first-run friction for two popular model providers.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires equal multi-provider models, Secret bindings, budget/data policy and offline/Demo operation.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT this domain shape. Reimplement through ModelProviderPort and SecretBinding, storing only binding IDs and discovered capabilities.
units.responsibilityConflict: A raw vendor key has no organization owner, permitted data/model, budget, expiry or accountable approval.
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL boundary flaw: the plaintext API key is returned inside ordinary domain configuration, inviting persistence/logging/export. Provider choice is hard-coded and lacks model, endpoint, organization, region, data-use, budget and rotation policy; password masking protects terminal echo only.

units.function: Selects file logging or a nonfunctional cloud option that falls back to file logging.
units.dependencyDirection: Prompt UI -> LoggingConfig and ambient local log directory.
units.keyDataModels: File mode and log path; cloud exists only as presentation.
units.lifecycle: Select mode, collect local path or show coming-soon note, always return file config.
units.testAssessment: No focused promptLogging test was found. Completed log-check evidence does not cover selection/fallback, retention or redaction.
units.designRationale: Advertise planned cloud logging while retaining an operational local fallback.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs explicit observability sinks, evidence/log separation, redaction, retention and residency.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT through ObservabilityPort and list only installed capabilities; never silently change the selected data destination.
units.responsibilityConflict: Logs can contain company/Agent/user data without a data owner, retention or export authorization.
units.securityFindings: The cloud choice is discarded and replaced by file logging, which can violate location/retention expectations. Arbitrary paths lack canonical, owner, mode, quota, rotation and symlink policy.

units.function: Chooses local encrypted, AWS, GCP or Vault Secret provider, strict references and an optional local key path.
units.dependencyDirection: Prompt UI -> shared provider enum/config; external provider health and migration live elsewhere.
units.keyDataModels: SecretProvider, strictMode and local key-file path.
units.lifecycle: Select provider and strictness, collect local path when relevant, warn about external integration, return config.
units.testAssessment: Completed Secret suite passed 8/8 for migration/provider surfaces and AWS root guidance; no focused prompt test proves unsupported-provider blocking, path safety or strict-mode implications.
units.designRationale: Make local encryption easy while exposing enterprise vault direction and discouraging root credentials.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs capability-discovered Secret providers, strict references, custody, rotation/versioning and Connector-specific delivery.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT provider selection and workload-identity guidance, but list only installed/healthy adapters and require migration preview/rollback for custody changes.
units.responsibilityConflict: Changing Secret custody is a high-risk organizational action, not a preference; no owner, migration scope or approval is captured.
units.securityFindings: HIGH: GCP and Vault remain selectable while explicitly unwired, allowing an invalid security configuration to be saved; strictMode defaults false. Local paths lack canonical/no-follow/owner checks. Positive: AWS credentials are directed to workload/runtime identity and raw credentials are not collected here.

units.function: Interactive network/auth profile selection for loopback, LAN, tailnet and custom private/public deployments.
units.dependencyDirection: Prompt UI -> hostname parser and server-bind composer -> shared bind predicates.
units.keyDataModels: Bind/deployment/exposure modes, host/port, allowed hostnames, public origin and UI flag.
units.lifecycle: Choose reachability and port; collect allowlist or custom auth/exposure/host/origin; compose config.
units.testAssessment: Completed network-bind suite passed 5/5 for loopback and missing-tailnet fallback. Prompt cases for authenticated/public/custom, adversarial URLs, proxies/TLS and cancellation are missing.
units.designRationale: Lead users toward safe localhost while progressively disclosing advanced network choices.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs closed deployment profiles enforcing auth/TLS/origin/proxy/signup invariants across CLI and runtime.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT progressive disclosure and the loopback guard, but enforce the same rules headlessly; separate bootstrap claim/signup and require HTTPS public origins outside development.
units.responsibilityConflict: Network/auth changes expose approval/evidence surfaces and require an accountable deployment administrator and auditable diff.
units.securityFindings: Positive: interactive local_trusted rejects non-loopback, mitigating the unsafe lower composer. HIGH: public URL accepts HTTP, embedded credentials, paths/query/fragments, localhost/private destinations and mismatch with bind/allowlist; signup remains enabled. Noninteractive callers bypass this prompt guard.

units.function: Chooses local disk or S3-compatible object storage and collects path, bucket, region, endpoint, prefix and addressing mode.
units.dependencyDirection: Prompt UI -> StorageConfig and ambient instance defaults; credentials/connectivity are deferred.
units.keyDataModels: Storage provider, local directory and S3 namespace/address settings.
units.lifecycle: Choose provider, collect local path or S3 fields, return config while preserving inactive settings.
units.testAssessment: No focused promptStorage test was found. Completed storage provider/check evidence does not validate this input flow, endpoint policy or credential custody.
units.designRationale: Support local-first and S3-compatible vendors without collecting cloud credentials into product config.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs data-location contracts, tenant namespaces, encryption, egress policy and validated credential-bound endpoints.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT through DataStore/ObjectStore ports with endpoint/TLS/namespace/encryption/residency validation and consented health checks.
units.responsibilityConflict: Storage changes move company evidence/data custody without an owner, migration plan, residency or export approval.
units.securityFindings: HIGH: arbitrary S3 endpoint lacks URL/scheme/TLS/private-network policy, enabling SSRF or ambient-credential forwarding. Bucket/region/prefix lack namespace and traversal rules; encryption/versioning/object-lock are absent. Local paths lack canonical/no-follow/permission/capacity policy.
